history.content: One of the parts of the brain affected by dementia is the frontal and temporal lobes, as seen in Frontotemporal Lobar Degeneration (FTLD). Additionally, the hippocampus is often damaged in Alzheimer's disease and other forms of dementia; short - term memory loss and disorientation are included among the early symptoms.
Is there effective medication for dementia?

Oral nicotinamide, a form of vitamin B (niacin), has not been found to have a clinically significant effect on Alzheimer's dementia, vascular dementia, or fronto-temporal dementia. However, niacin intake from foods is inversely associated with Alzheimer's disease. Folic acid supplementation has been found to improve the memory of older people and lower blood homocysteine levels, but its effect on reducing the risk of cognitive impairment in the older population is still a subject of debate. Research continues into other areas where specific statins also appear to have a favorable effect including dementia.  However, an effective medication for dementia has not been found yet.

Repeated concussions and possibly sub-concussive head impacts can increase a person's risk in later life for CTE (chronic traumatic encephalopathy) and mental health issues such as dementia, Parkinson's disease, and depression.  CTE had been described in boxers, football players and other professional athletes.  Professional American football players self - reporting concussions are at greater risk for having depressive episodes later in life compared with those retired players self - reporting no concussions.

For example, the case of Mike Webster, a former Pittsburgh Steelers player, was a catalyst for increased awareness of CTE. Webster suffered from cognitive and intellectual impairment, destitution, mood disorders, depression, drug abuse, and suicide attempts in his later life. An autopsy conducted by Dr. Bennet Omalu revealed large accumulations of tau protein in Webster's brain, which are associated with dementia and mood changes, similar to the way clumps of beta-amyloid protein contribute to Alzheimer's disease.  In a 1987 study of former Norwegian association football national team players, one third of the players were found to have central cerebral atrophy.  The main types of football are association football, American football, Canadian football, Australian rules football, Gaelic football, rugby league and rugby union.
Are they taking some measures to prevent?   This is a very dismal fact!

Yes, there are measures being taken, for instance, various programs like USA Football's "Heads Up Football" aim to reduce concussions by teaching coaches and players about the signs of a concussion, proper equipment fitting, and tackling methods that avoid helmet-to-helmet contact.  However, a study in the Orthopaedic Journal of Sports Medicine found that Heads Up Football was ineffective.  Another organization, Pop Warner Little Scholars, has implemented more extensive reforms that have been effective in significantly reducing concussion rates.
In addition to these programs, advancements have been made in football helmet design to make them safer and better at absorbing impacts.  A joint effort between Virginia Tech and Wake Forest has been testing current football helmets and giving them yearly ratings since 2011. On a scale out of 5 stars, only one helmet was awarded a 5 in 2011. In 2012, two additional helmet designs were awarded 5 stars.
